thread.title: Sonos Stock Coverage Initiated With Mix Of Buys And Holds

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Sonos Stock Coverage Initiated With Mix Of Buys And Holds
text:
Several Wall Street analysts on Monday initiated coverage of recent IPO Sonos ( SONO ) but were split on their assessments of the stock.
X Some are positive on Sonos stock while others are neutral on the maker of premium audio speakers, which went public Aug. 2 at $15 a share. Sonos stock hit a record high of 23.60 on its second day of trading. It has been forming an IPO base for the past three-plus weeks.
Sonos stock fell 6.4% to close at 18.92 on the stock market today .
Six brokerage firms started coverage of Sonos on Monday. Three gave it buy ratings and three gave it hold ratings.

Sonos Supports Multiple Voice Assistants "We view Sonos' connected home speaker technology enabled with multiple voice assistants as a differentiated value proposition that should help Sonos to hold its own in a competitive smart speaker market," Goldman analyst Rod Hall said in a report. He rates the stock as buy with a 12-month price target of 25.
Sonos also possesses valuable multiroom music streaming technology that should give it an edge over rivals, Hall said.
Competitors in the smart speaker market include Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google.
Sonos' revenue growth this year will be driven by wireless speakers and home theater speakers. It launched the Sonos One speaker last October and the Sonos Beam in July.
Not Another Fitbit Or GoPro RBC analyst Amit Daryanani started Sonos with an outperform rating and a price target of 25.
Sonos should benefit from strong customer engagement, growth in the music streaming business and its open platform approach, he said in a report. Its devices support voice assistants from Amazon and Google.
Sonos won't be another Fitbit ( FIT ) or GoPro ( GPRO ), Daryanani said. Those consumer electronics companies saw a strong initial surge in popularity but waned as customers lost interest in their products.
"Sonos' user engagement looks very strong," he said. "On average, customers listen to about 70 hours of content per month and about 80% more music after purchasing their first Sonos product. Nearly half of Sonos' 7 million households open the Sonos app daily."
Needs To Move Into New Markets Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty initiated Sonos coverage with an equal-weight rating and price target of 20.
Huberty said she is cautious on Sonos until it can show evidence that its move into adjacent markets is working.
"To maintain differentiation in a crowded $18 billion home-audio market, Sonos must leverage its technology stack to expand into new-use cases for new and existing households," she said in a report.
Moving from stand-alone music speakers and into speakers for home theater systems was a first step. Outdoor speakers are likely to follow soon, Huberty said.
